purpose: Three.js lesson and proof-stage illustration design/audit; not a claim that every proposed preset is implemented.
indexing: proofIndex is zero-based; sceneKey is lessonId; renderer may route through modelFamily or existingModelKey.
renderingRequirements: Keep the existing flat reader and 18px body text.
Use in-flow Three.js illustrations, no workbench or dashboard redesign.
Do not reuse a figure if objective, feasible set, variable role or numeric parameters conflict.
Match a proof-stage preset only when its mathematical objects are actually rendered.
Always show exact formula, assumption, axis meaning and limitation; geometry supplements proofs.
Render one-dimensional diagrams as labeled thin slices; decorative thickness is not an optimization variable.
Primal and dual spaces require separate labeled views.
Infinity and open endpoints need explicit notation, never finite-height approximations presented as exact.

lessons.assumptions: C² on an open region containing the segment; short-step statement is local.

lessons.concreteModel: Compare A=diag(1,2), b=(2,2) against A=[1,1], b=2: unique bowl versus flat minimum line x1+x2=2.
lessons.assumptions: Real finite matrix A; no full rank assumption for existence; full column rank for uniqueness.

lessons.concreteModel: Triangle C={x≥0,x1+x2≤2}; draw feasible segments, supporting halfspaces, affine preimage ellipse, and disconnected intervals counterexample.
lessons.assumptions: t∈[0,1]; nonnegative weights sum to one.
lessons.limitation: A clipped halfspace is not a bounded set; one segment verifies only one instance.

lessons.concreteModel: f=||x||²; endpoints (0,0),(2,0), t∈[0,1]; epigraph points above surface and sublevel disk. Separate f(x)=x³ counterexample.
lessons.assumptions: Convex domain and t∈[0,1); endpoints with finite values; extend to t=1 by equality.
lessons.limitation: Infinity of indicator is encoded by excluded domain, never a large finite wall; cubic counterexample is a separate function.

lessons.concreteModel: f=||x||²/2; secants approach tangent at x, support at interpolation z, compare gradient arrows at x and y.
lessons.assumptions: Differentiable f on open convex domain; segment stays inside.
lessons.limitation: Perspective cannot establish global support or monotonicity; numeric samples are illustrative.

lessons.concreteModel: f=(x1²+4x2²)/2, μ=1; directional slices and quadratic support; separately show x⁴ at origin for nonuniform curvature.
lessons.assumptions: C² on open convex domain; uniform Hessian lower bound μI with μ>0 for strong convexity.
lessons.limitation: Strict convexity is not uniform strong convexity; uniqueness conditional on existence unless coercivity is established.

lessons.concreteModel: Use max{(x-1)²,(x+1)²}, nonnegative sums, affine compositions; F(x,y)=(x-y)²+y² has marginal x²/2 along y=x/2.
lessons.assumptions: Nonnegative weights; monotone convex outer function; jointly convex F; finite marginal values in proof.
lessons.limitation: Minimum of convex functions need not be convex. Exact marginal example does not establish approximate-minimizer arguments.

lessons.concreteModel: Use f(x)=x² on C=[1,∞): optimum at 1 and nonzero derivative 2; mark nearby feasible chords and supporting slope.
lessons.assumptions: Convex nonempty C and convex f; differentiability for first-order equivalence.
lessons.limitation: Local-to-global contradiction is general reasoning, not a claim that the plotted bowl proves every convex function case.

lessons.concreteModel: Plot |x| with supporting lines gx, g∈[-1,1], then l1 pyramid; separate -sqrt(x) at x=0.
lessons.assumptions: Proper convex function, support inequality over full domain.
lessons.limitation: No finite steep slope is a subgradient of -sqrt at zero. Fan sampling does not prove the entire interval.

lessons.concreteModel: F(u)=1/2(u-b)²+λ|u|, λ≥0; overlay smooth gradient and allowable penalty slopes, threshold b at ±λ.
lessons.assumptions: f differentiable convex; h proper convex; points in common domain.
lessons.limitation: Input b is a parameter, not another optimized variable; show support inequalities before summing.

lessons.concreteModel: Disk projection of u=(3,4), R=2 plus separate halfspace a=(1,1), b=2.
lessons.assumptions: Nonempty closed convex C in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
lessons.limitation: Existing disk model cannot stand in for the halfspace formula; normal arrows belong to the variable plane.

lessons.concreteModel: Triangle C; compare interior, edge and vertex normal cones; project two inputs and compare distances; add projected-gradient fixed point.
lessons.assumptions: C nonempty closed convex; convex differentiable objective for optimality equivalence; t>0.
lessons.limitation: A normal cone at a corner is not one normal vector. Show both input and projected segments on the same scale.

lessons.concreteModel: f(x)=x²/2 gives f*(y)=y²/2; support intercept -f*(y), gap=(x-y)²/2. Separate λ|x| slopes outside [-λ,λ].
lessons.assumptions: Proper convex f; finite values for finite gap; Q positive definite in inverse formula.
lessons.limitation: x and dual y are distinct variables in distinct roles; unbounded supremum is indicated by an escaping ray, not a finite cap.

lessons.concreteModel: min x² with x≥1: L=x²+λ(1-x), g=λ-λ²/4, λ≥0; optimum x=1, λ=2.
lessons.assumptions: Primal feasibility and λ≥0 are essential for the lower-bound chain.
lessons.limitation: Do not minimize jointly over x and λ; dual is maxλ minx. An infeasible primal point gives no gap certificate.

lessons.concreteModel: For f=x²,c=1-x, perturbation set is r>max(1-u,0)², with support r≥1-2u touching (0,1); mark strict feasible x=2. Separate exp(x) nonattainment.
lessons.assumptions: Use exact full-space finite convex assumptions and full-row-rank A from lesson; finite p*.
lessons.limitation: This no-equality 2D slice illustrates separation only. It cannot visualize arbitrary equality perturbations, prove openness, or replace the Slater proof.

lessons.concreteModel: Existing halfspace quadratic center (2,2), constraint x1+x2≤B, optimum ((B/2),(B/2)) for B<4; λ=(4-B)/2 and V=(4-B)²/4.
lessons.assumptions: Convex differentiable objective/inequalities; affine equalities; Slater needed for stated necessity.
lessons.limitation: Gradient and constraint normals are in variable space, not surface normals; sensitivity gives a subgradient, derivative only when differentiable.

lessons.concreteModel: f=(x1²+8x2²)/2, L=8; show Q_L at x and trial gradient steps, including too-large steps and Armijo line.
lessons.assumptions: L-Lipschitz gradient on segment; 0<t≤1/L for standard t/2 decrease.
lessons.limitation: The existing gradient trajectory does not itself show the upper model or integration proof.

lessons.concreteModel: Same SPD quadratic with t=1/8; show Δk, Dk/(2t), one-step released distance budget, telescoping cancellation and 1/k bound.
lessons.assumptions: Convex L-smooth f; attained minimizer; 0<t≤1/L.
lessons.limitation: A strongly convex example may converge faster than 1/k; observed rate is not the general worst-case guarantee.

lessons.concreteModel: f=(x1²+8x2²)/2, μ=1,L=8; lower bowl minimized at x-g/μ; compare actual gaps with (7/8)^kΔ0.
lessons.assumptions: Global μ-strong convexity and L-smoothness; exact gradient steps t=1/L.
lessons.limitation: Distance factor and objective factor are different; μ,L cannot be inferred from perspective distortion.

lessons.concreteModel: f=(x1²+100x2²)/2; D=diag(1,.1), physical x0=(1,1), transformed z0=(1,10).
lessons.assumptions: SPD Q; 0<t<2/L for convergence; invertible D.
lessons.limitation: Changing axes changes numerical distances; do not compare apparent screen widths as condition numbers.

lessons.concreteModel: h(u)=|u|, J=|u|+(u-v)²/(2t), t>0; show affine minorant, coercive lower parabola and unique minimum, then projection special case.
lessons.assumptions: Proper closed convex h in finite-dimensional Euclidean space; t>0.
lessons.limitation: A particular h cannot establish existence of an affine minorant for every proper closed convex function.

lessons.concreteModel: Threshold a=tλ; show fixed-input sections for v>a, v<-a, and |v|≤a; compare ridge u=S_a(v) to u=v/(1+tλ).
lessons.assumptions: t>0 and λ≥0; scalar separability used coordinatewise.
lessons.limitation: v is a parameter; existing prox model assumes t=1 and needs explicit rescaling for arbitrary t.

lessons.concreteModel: F(u)=(u-3)²/2+|u|, L=1; show Q_t-F=(1/t-1)(u-x)²/2, t≤1; trace proximal gradient.
lessons.assumptions: Convex differentiable L-smooth f, proper closed convex h; attained optimizer for rate; t≤1/L.
lessons.limitation: Thickness is not a variable. Include distance budget in an inset rather than suggesting surface descent alone proves the rate.

lessons.concreteModel: A=diag(1,2), b=(3,.4), λ=1; primal optimum (2,0), value 2.58; dual rectangle |y1|≤1, |2y2|≤1; optimal y=(1,.4).
lessons.assumptions: λ>0; t≤1/||A||²; gap uses feasible dual y.
lessons.limitation: Primal and dual points must never be plotted as if in the same variable space; use separate clearly labeled scene/preset.

axes: true objective and local quadratic model
lessons.concreteModel: Existing SPD quadratic gives exact full Newton step. Add nonquadratic f=x²/2+x⁴/4 for local-error behavior; damped steps and Armijo test.
lessons.assumptions: Positive-definite Hessian for descent; uniform inverse bound and Lipschitz Hessian near x* for local quadratic estimate.
lessons.limitation: Quadratic model has zero Newton error and cannot demonstrate generic local quadratic convergence.

axes: phi_t(x), or objective height with path
lessons.concreteModel: Triangle benchmark f=((x1-2)²+4(x2-1)²)/2; phi_t=tf-log(x1)-log(x2)-log(2-x1-x2); exact center path.
lessons.assumptions: Strict interior nonempty; convex differentiable constraints; exact center with stationarity for m/t certificate.
lessons.limitation: Clip display near boundary without implying finite barrier there; a single Newton step is not an exact center.

lessons.concreteModel: f=(x-3)²/2,h=(z+1)²/2; x=z optimum 1 and value 4. Show sequential block moves and separate primal/dual residual curves.
lessons.assumptions: Exact block minimization; ρ>0; scaled u=y/ρ.
lessons.limitation: Multiplier u is not a third primal coordinate; nonfeasible objective below 4 is not improvement of feasible optimum.

lessons.concreteModel: C={x≥0,x1+x2≤2}; Euclidean projection a=(2,1) is (1.5,.5), objective .625; H-projection is (1.2,.8), objective .4.
lessons.assumptions: H=diag(1,4) positive definite; accurately computed projections; common feasible objective comparison.
lessons.limitation: Existing isotropic KKT bowl is not this anisotropic benchmark. Algorithms need equal feasibility and certificate criteria, not just trajectories.

lessons.concreteModel: Same triangle benchmark; x*=(6/5,4/5), λ*=4/5; decompose gap into d1²/2+2d2²+(4/5)(2-x1-x2).
lessons.assumptions: x feasible; nonnegativity of all three certificate terms; η*=0.
lessons.limitation: A finite mesh is not the global certificate; preserve the exact sum-of-nonnegative-terms identity beside figure.

lessons.assumptions: Specific starting point and preserved projection branch; arbitrary input projection also needs clipping negative components.
lessons.limitation: The exact 3/8 recurrence is not valid for all starts or all projection active sets.

axes: objective / barrier height in separate view
lessons.concreteModel: From (1,1), active Newton p=(1/5,-1/5). Barrier example step ends (46/53,42/53), slack18/53; ADMM fixed point uses u*=(.8,.8), z*=x*.
lessons.assumptions: Check active constraints and feasibility; exact center required for 3/t; ADMM fixed point is not a finite convergence claim.
lessons.limitation: Do not label the displayed one-step barrier endpoint a center or give it the exact-center gap.

axes: changes per independent exercise; label every switch
lessons.concreteModel: Six independent presets: rank-one bowl (x1+x2)²; scalar upper-bound KKT; diag(2,8) gradient; threshold .75; triangle projection; singleton feasible x²≤0.
lessons.assumptions: Each exercise has independent objective, domain, parameters and coordinate meanings.
lessons.limitation: Do not carry L, Hessian, objective or axis labels between exercises. Singleton feasible set has no Slater point and no finite KKT multiplier.
